questions.text: A classroom desk fits an average seated student but fails students carrying bags through the aisle. Which correction best matches the source map?

options.text: Anthropometric review must include dynamic movement, not only static body size.
Average dimensions are always enough once a seat fits.
Only color and texture can solve the aisle problem.
The issue is purely historical style, not human fit.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 connects body dimensions to movement, activity, and rest, not just static fit.
rationale.takeaway: Anthropometrics must be tested in use, not only in a static diagram.
rationale.b: The source warns that averages require caution.
rationale.c: Surface treatment does not replace movement clearance.
rationale.d: Human fit is the core issue here.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 connects body dimensions to movement, activity, and rest, not just static fit. Anthropometrics must be tested in use, not only in a static diagram.

questions.text: Which statement best defines anthropometrics for architectural use?

options.text: It is the study of color hue and chroma.
It is the symbolic role of social distance only.
It is the legal process for issuing building permits.
It measures the size and proportions of the human body to inform space and form.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 defines anthropometry as measurement of body size and proportions.
rationale.a: Hue and chroma belong to color vocabulary.
rationale.c: Building permits are outside the anthropometrics definition.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 defines anthropometry as measurement of body size and proportions. Anthropometrics starts with body measurement.

questions.text: Why should a designer be cautious when using average body dimensions?

options.text: Averages are prohibited in all architectural design.
Real users vary by age, sex, group, and individual body differences.
Averages work only for exterior facades.
Variation matters only for decorative color choices.

rationale.correct: The local source explicitly warns that variation from the norm always exists.
rationale.takeaway: Average dimensions are references, not guarantees.
rationale.a: Averages can be useful starting points when tested carefully.
rationale.c: Interior and exterior environments both involve users.
rationale.d: Variation is a body-fit issue, not merely color preference.

questions.explanation: The local source explicitly warns that variation from the norm always exists. Average dimensions are references, not guarantees.

questions.text: A reception counter is sized for reach, visibility, writing posture, and short waiting tasks. Which concept best describes this broader coordination?

options.text: Visual scale only, because the counter appears large.
The ken only, because every counter is a Japanese module.
Shadow texture only, because the counter casts shade.
Ergonomics, because it coordinates environments with physiological and psychological capacities.

rationale.correct: TOA 2 defines ergonomics as coordinating devices, systems, and environments with human capacities and requirements.
rationale.takeaway: Ergonomics turns body data into usable task conditions.
rationale.a: Visual scale does not cover task posture and reach by itself.
rationale.b: The ken is a specific modular precedent, not every dimensioning problem.
rationale.c: Shadow does not resolve ergonomic task fit.

questions.explanation: TOA 2 defines ergonomics as coordinating devices, systems, and environments with human capacities and requirements. Ergonomics turns body data into usable task conditions.

questions.text: A plan provides chair clearances but ignores the social distance needed for conversation. Which paired concepts should be separated?

options.text: Anthropometrics covers color, while proxemics covers structural load.
Both concepts mean exactly the same thing.
Neither concept relates to people in space.
Anthropometrics covers body fit, while proxemics covers personal and social spacing.

rationale.correct: The source map links body dimensions to movement/rest and social distances/personal space as a related but distinct concern.
rationale.takeaway: A good human-fit answer often distinguishes body envelope from interpersonal spacing.
rationale.a: Color and structural load are separate vocabularies.
rationale.b: The concepts overlap in use but are not identical.
